_meta.source: USDA FoodData Central (fdc.nal.usda.gov) reference values, hand-curated for this seed pipeline
_meta.note: Values are per 100g of the ingredient in its common raw/generic form (cooked where noted), rounded to typical published precision. Hand-curated rather than fetched live from the USDA API, so seeding stays offline and deterministic. Keys are the exact normalized ingredient name strings produced by mealsight.matching.normalize.normalize_ingredient (the same normalizer the runtime matcher uses), chosen to reach at least 80% distinct-ingredient coverage and 95% occurrence-weighted coverage across the seeded recipe corpus (see seed/load_nutrition.py's coverage report). Expanded in the Phase 2.2 nutrition-coverage remediation from an initial 136-entry set that only guaranteed coverage of ingredients appearing in 5+ recipes; a handful of keys here are verbatim garbled ingredient names from the source recipe text (e.g. accented characters stripped by the normalizer) rather than correctly spelled words, kept that way deliberately so the key exactly matches what the normalizer produces for that recipe text.
_meta.units: calories in kcal, protein/carbs/fat/fiber in grams, sodium in milligrams, all per 100g
_meta.provenance: PROVENANCE AND INTENDED USE: The original 136 entries (present before the Phase 2.2 coverage-remediation expansion) were hand-curated with reference to real USDA FoodData Central figures. The 373 entries added during that expansion are typical per-100g estimates for each ingredient's common form, drawn from general nutrition-science knowledge rather than individually verified against a live USDA FoodData Central lookup for each specific item. None of these values — old or new — were independently fact-checked against USDA source records entry-by-entry as part of that expansion. They are approximations suitable for relative comparison within this application (e.g. estimating whether a recipe leans high-protein or high-calorie, comparing recipes against each other) and are NOT suitable for clinical, medical, allergen-safety, or other precision-nutrition use. Anyone needing verified figures for a specific ingredient should look it up directly in USDA FoodData Central rather than trusting this file as an authoritative source.
